name: Intego
tagline: Mac antivirus, firewall, cleanup, backup, and parental controls

pricing.native: Annual licence; current bundle price varies
pricing.notes: The pricing model is not safely comparable as one fixed monthly USD amount. Review the official source before publication.

tiers.name: VirusBarrier X9
tiers.limits: 1, 3 or 5 Mac licenses depending on checkout selection
tiers.notes: Official European campaign pages show a regular €24.99/year (about $28.89 at €1 = $1.156); the active promotional USD price was not stable enough to record.

tiers.name: Mac Internet Security X9
tiers.limits: 1, 3 or 5 Macs; antivirus plus firewall/network protection
tiers.notes: Official campaigns conflict between €19.99 and €24.99 for the first payment (about $23.11–$28.89), then €49.99/year (about $57.79).

tiers.name: Mac Premium Bundle X9
tiers.limits: 1, 3 or 5 Macs; antivirus, firewall, cleanup, backup and parental-control tools
tiers.notes: Official campaigns conflict between €34.99 and €39.99 first payment (about $40.45–$46.23), then €84.99/year (about $98.25).

pricing.billingTerms: annual or 2-year billing; promotional price applies only to the first payment
pricing.hiddenCosts: Price changes with the number of Macs and term; first-payment promotions renew at a much higher regular price, VAT can be added, and optional VPN or other services are separate

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Intego's durable value is security, infrastructure, trust, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a local diagnostic or backup companion for Mac security suite; do not claim to replace audited security, identity, VPN, or cloud-storage infrastructure.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: global network or redundant storage infrastructure
whyPeopleStillPay: Intego: Security subscriptions buy professional operations, audits, response capacity, redundancy, and accountability when something goes wrong.
ongoingBurden: Own threat modelling, key management, patching, backups, restore tests, incident response, privacy requests, and dependency security.

priorArt.name: Duplicati
priorArt.desc: Encrypted backup client for local and cloud targets.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Kopia
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Excellent encrypted backup; it does nothing for malware, firewalling, cleanup, or parental controls.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Malwarebytes Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free scanner cleans malware on demand; firewall, continuous protection, backup, cleanup, and parental controls are absent.

notes: Credibility row: Intego survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Intego; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Go 1.24 + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a local diagnostic or backup companion for Mac security suite; do not claim to replace audited security, identity, VPN, or cloud-storage infrastructure.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: identity, credit, or broker-removal operations; recovery guarantees and regulated trust; audited cryptography and incident response.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
